lead: Core review 1 (21 October 2026), the second run of the queue. The boundary test of the scaffold prompts is now a distribution: the 95th percentile of the boundary distances at most 3 game px AND the largest distance at most 6 game px (the old rule took the largest distance alone and refused good pictures for one thin protrusion). The scaffold's geometry wins: parts the lit scaffold shows are painted as shown, whatever a prompt says about a hidden front. Each prompt starts with a CORE REVIEW 1 header that says so.

Done and accepted (not on this page any more): Big Station, Big Farm Halt, Town hall and Warehouse (all twelve views) and the windmill body r0. Core's decisions on every refused attempt are in codex-queue/status/CORE-REVIEW-1.md on branch claude/codex-queue.

Each group below is ONE Codex conversation: paste its prompts one after another, each after the previous one finishes. The button Copy whole conversation copies the group's prompts in order, with a separator line between them; Copy prompt copies a single one.

Codex works in the main checkout (G:DEVTerepasztal	erepasztal), which has one branch checked out at a time. So run ONE group at a time there. Two groups can run at the same time only if Codex gives each its own git worktree. Every group is on its own branch, except that the Later prompt C33b belongs to the Rotations conversation (same branch, art/535-rotations).

Turned views are painted over Core's 3D scaffolds (branch claude/art-scaffolds-review-2, head fc07d589); each prompt says how to read them. The narrow depot (C35a) waits for a Blender blockout scaffold that Core is making. Accepted pictures are not painted again.

groups.title: Rotations over scaffolds
groups.run: C18a, C22a, C19a and C20a are done: all twelve views are accepted, so they are no longer listed. Paste CR1-adopt first (it only marks five accepted views in prompts.json), then the larger plants, the house, and the hydro plant r0 last (it stops after r0; if r0 fails the fallback is a blockout scaffold from Core). The branch already holds twelve jobs from 19 October: each prompt rebases before it pushes.
